title: Comparing Experiences: képest, egyre, and the Full Toolkit

sections.title: Five lessons, one reflection
sections.content: You now have language for the whole arc of talking about an experience: whether it ever happened (már, még soha nem), whether it was a first (először), what it did to the person or thing it touched (participle adjectives like elkészített, megérintett), and how things have changed since (azelőtt, azóta, visszatekintve). Comparing experiences adds one more piece: putting two things — then and now, you and someone else — side by side.

items.spanish: A mai önbizalmamhoz képest, régen nagyon félénk voltam.
items.english: Compared to my confidence today, I used to be very shy.

items.spanish: Egyre bátrabb lettem, minél többször próbáltam ki új dolgokat.
items.english: I became increasingly braver, the more often I tried new things.

items.spanish: A mostani utam sokkal izgalmasabb volt, mint az első.
items.english: This trip was much more exciting than the first one.

sections.content: képest always needs a noun in the -hoz/-hez/-höz case in front of it, even when that noun is just a pronoun like ehhez ("to this") or ahhoz ("to that") — ehhez képest, ahhoz képest, a régi énemhez képest. Leave that case ending off and képest has nothing to compare against.
